title: Authorization Flowbook — Access, Procurement & Travel
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Summary:
This Flowbook consolidates company-wide procedures for granting access and permissions, approving changes, managing data and retention, processing procurement and expenses, onboarding vendors, and authorizing business travel. The intent is to provide a single, actionable reference for requesters, approvers, and operational teams so approvals are fast, auditable, and aligned with security and budget guardrails.

Scope:
- Applies to all Redwood employees, contractors, and vendors who request access to systems, submit purchase requests, propose configuration or code changes, or travel on company business.
- Excludes purely personal reimbursements (see People Ops T&E exceptions) and one-off low-value reimbursements under $25.

Principles:
1) Least privilege: Grant the minimum access required and review every 90 days for non-admin roles.
2) Separation of duties: Requesters cannot self-approve purchases, access, or change deployments that materially affect their own services.
3) Risk-based approvals: Higher risk (data access, high dollar spend, code push to prod) requires stronger review.
4) Auditability: All requests must include business justification and be logged in central systems (AccessHub / ProcPortal).

Roles and Ownership:
- Requester: initiates the request with justification, cost center, and business owner.
- Approver: the named manager or cost-center owner; senior approver required for high-risk items.
- Security owner: reviews data-access and vendor security questionnaires.
- Procurement: validates vendor terms and preferred supplier status for purchases > $5k.
- Finance: verifies budget and issues PO for approved purchases.
- IT Ops / SRE: executes access provisioning, change coordination, and rollback if needed.

Access & Permissions:
Request flow:
1. Create an access request in AccessHub with: resource, role, duration, justification, business owner, and confidentiality level.
2. Immediate manager approval required for all requests.
3. Security owner review for any request that: grants access to PII, allows export, or touches model training data.
4. Audit tag assigned if request is >90 days or privileged.

Approval matrix (summary):
| Resource classification | Typical approver | Security review required | Auto-expiry |
|------------------------|------------------|-------------------------|-------------|
| Public docs            | Manager          | No                      | 365 days    |
| Internal non-sensitive | Manager          | No                      | 90 days     |
| Confidential (PII)     | Manager + SecOps | Yes                     | 30 days     |
| Admin/system-level     | Manager + IT Ops | Yes                     | 14 days     |

Re-certification:
- Every 90 days an automated recertification email is sent for non-admin roles. Unattended roles will be disabled after 14 days of non-response.

Emergency access (break-glass):
- Temporarily granted via Emergency Access form with post-hoc justification and 24-hour security debrief. Any break-glass must be recorded and reviewed within 3 business days.

Change Management:
Change categories:
- Routine: low-risk config changes (non-prod) — schedule in regular maintenance window, manager approval.
- Standard: pre-approved, repeatable changes (e.g., certificate rotation) — CAB notification.
- Significant: code or infra changes impacting production — requires SRE sign-off and change runbook.
- Emergency: incident-driven changes — use Emergency Change process and record rollback plan.

Change procedure (significant changes):
1. Create Change Request (CR) in ChangeTracker with: description, owners, rollback plan, risk assessment, and test plan.
2. SRE and Product sign-off required.
3. Schedule canary and phased rollout with feature flags; communicate to oncall.
4. Post-deploy validation tasks and metrics to confirm behavior.
5. Post-change review within 5 business days; capture learnings in ChangeTracker.

Rollback criteria:
- Error rate > 1% above baseline for 10 minutes, latency SLO breach > 50ms increase, or critical customer impact. Pre-deploy canary thresholds must be defined in the CR.

Data Management:
Classification levels:
- Public: safe for external distribution.
- Internal: Redwood operational content; acceptable for internal collaboration.
- Confidential: employee PII, customer data, model training datasets.
- Restricted: regulated data (PCI, HIPAA).

Storage and handling rules:
- Confidential and Restricted data must be stored in approved buckets with customer-managed encryption keys (KMS) and VPC-only access.
- Mask or tokenize PII before exporting from platform systems.
- Data retention: standard logs 90 days; model training datasets retention to be defined per project (default 2 years). Exceptions require Data Steward approval.

Data access review:
- Any dataset that contains Confidential or Restricted data must have an explicit Data Owner and an access approval recorded in AccessHub.

Procurement & Expenses:
Thresholds and approvals table:
| Amount (USD) | Required approvers | Procurement involvement |
|--------------|--------------------|------------------------|
| <$1,000      | Manager            | Optional               |
| $1,000–$5,000| Manager + Finance  | Procurement advisory   |
| $5,000–$50,000 | Manager + Procurement + Finance | Procurement required |
| >$50,000     | Exec sponsor + Procurement + Legal + Finance | Procurement & Legal required |

Preferred vendors and contract reuse:
- Procurement maintains a Preferred Supplier list. For common categories (cloud, GPUs, security tooling), use pre-negotiated contracts when possible to speed approvals.

Purchase flow (typical):
1. Requester submits Purchase Request in ProcPortal including SOW, vendor info, and business justification.
2. Procurement validates vendor terms and negotiates as needed for >$5k.
3. Finance confirms budget.
4. Legal reviews contract when >$50k or if non-standard clauses present.
5. PO issued; vendor is approved for payment.

Expense & Travel policy (high level):
- All business travel requires pre-approval via TravelRequest with estimated cost and trip purpose.
- Use company booking tool for flights; seat-class policy: economy for flights < 6 hours, premium-economy or equivalent on longer flights with manager approval.
- Per diem and per-trip lodging caps are published on the travel portal and vary by region (sample table below).

Travel caps by region (sample):
| Region | Daily per diem | Hotel cap/night |
|--------|----------------|-----------------|
| US     | $75            | $250            |
| EMEA   | 55 EUR         | 180 EUR         |
| APAC   | 8,000 JPY      | 25,000 JPY      |

Reimbursement timeline:
- Submit expense reports within 10 business days of trip end with receipts attached. Finance processes standard claims within 7 business days. Non-compliant items may be denied.

Vendor Management:
Onboarding checklist (minimum items):
- Vendor profile in VendorRegistry (legal name, tax ID, address).
- Security questionnaire completed (AIC or equivalent).
- Data processing agreement (DPA) signed if vendor processes Confidential or Restricted data.
- Insurance certificates verified for material engagements.
- SLAs and escalation contacts recorded.

Ongoing vendor reviews:
- Annual security attestation for vendors handling Confidential data.
- Quarterly contract performance review for strategic suppliers.

Templates and Examples:
- Purchase request JSON (sample):
{
  "requester": "alice@redwood.com",
  "cost_center": "AI-TEAM-01",
  "vendor": "CloudGpus Ltd",
  "amount": "15000",
  "justification": "Dedicated GPU pool for model benchmarking"
}

- Access request example (form fields): resource, role, start_date, end_date, business_justification, approvals (manager, security if required).

- Change request checklist: description, owners, test plan, canary plan, rollback steps, monitoring runbook, communication list.

Operational controls and automation:
- All request systems must emit an event to the central audit log with metadata: request_id, requester, approvers, timestamps, and attachments.
- Automated guardrails: requests exceeding policy thresholds trigger a hold and a notification to Procurement and Security.

Exceptions and escalation:
- To request an exception (policy deviation), open an Exception Request in the Policy Portal with rationale, compensating controls, and a 90-day review cadence.
- Appeals: a three-person committee (Finance, Security, and Requester’s leader) reviews exceptions within 5 business days.

Enforcement and compliance:
- Random quarterly audits will be performed against a sample of access, procurement, and travel records. Findings may lead to disciplinary action or process revisions.

Appendix A — Quick links (internal):
- AccessHub: https://internal.accesshub.redwood/requests
- ProcPortal: https://internal.procportal.redwood/purchase-requests
- ChangeTracker: https://internal.change.redwood/changes
- VendorRegistry: https://internal.vendorregistry.redwood/vendors

Appendix B — Contact matrix:
- Procurement: procurement@redwood.com
- Finance: finance-ops@redwood.com
- Security: secops@redwood.com
- Travel support: travel@redwood.com

Revision history:
- 2026-06-15: Initial published version (A. Patel).
- 2026-09-01: Updated travel caps and procurement threshold clarifications (reviewers: D. Kim, S. Martinez).

Related resources and next steps:
- For implementers: integrate request webhooks to central audit log and enable automated expiry on AccessHub.
- Recommend cross-functional tabletop exercise to validate Emergency Change and Break-Glass procedures within the next quarter.

End of Flowbook.
